result.markdown: # Create S3 & Push Data {.unnumbered} This is the third part of lab 7. It assumes you've set up your AWS group, user, configured the CLI, set up and launched an EC2 instance. In this lab, we'll create an S3 bucket and pushed the penguin `vetiver` model data.[^lab7-part-02] [^lab7-part-02]: If you haven't completed these steps, please see [Getting started with AWS](start-aws.qmd) and [EC2 Buckets](aws-ec2.qmd) ## Creating S3 buckets We can use the `s3api` command to create the S3 bucket for the `penguin-vetiver-model-data`. ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3api create-bucket \ --bucket penguin-vetiver-model-data \ --region us-east-1 \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: These commands are pretty straightforward, but you can also read more in the documentation.[^aws-s3-buckets] Note that bucket names must be globally unique. The response from the API should be something like the following: ```json { "Location": "/penguin-vetiver-model-data", "BucketArn": "arn:aws:s3:::penguin-vetiver-model-data" } ``` [^aws-s3-buckets]: Read more about creating S3 buckets in [Creating a general purpose bucket ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/create-bucket-overview.html) We can also see this in the dashboard by looking up **S3** resources: ![General purpose S3 bucket](img/lab7-s3-bucket-dashboard.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ## Pushing the models to S3 Now that we've created an S3 bucket, we can push the respective Python/R model data into their S3 locations. I'm going to keep the same `Python/` and `R/` folder structure, which I've displayed below:[^lab7-code-files] ```{.default} Python/ ├── Dockerfile ├── mod-api.py ├── model.py ├── models/ │ └── penguin_model/ │ └── 20260618T104900Z-91fdd/ │ ├── data.txt │ └── penguin_model.joblib ├── my-db.duckdb ├── README.md ├── requirements-api.txt └── requirements.txt 4 directories, 9 files ``` ```{.default} R/ ├── Dockerfile ├── model.R ├── models/ │ └── penguin_model/ │ └── 20260709T053628Z-09946/ │ ├── data.txt │ └── penguin_model.rds ├── my-db.duckdb ├── plumber.R ├── README.md ├── renv/ └── renv.lock 10 directories, 10 files ``` [^lab7-code-files]: These are the [code files](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab07) from [lab 4](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/tree/main/_labs/lab06). ### Python model From a Terminal in the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 cp Python/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ \ --recursive \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### R model From a Terminal in the `do4ds-labs/_labs/lab07` folder: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 cp R/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ \ --recursive \ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Copy vs. sync It might make more sense to use `sync` instead of copy. `sync` only uploads new/changed files, which might be better for repeated deploys: **`Python/`**: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 sync Python/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models/ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: **`R/`**: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 sync R/models/ s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/R/models/ --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: ### Verify The commands below will verify the model data has been put in the S3 bucket: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} aws s3 ls s3://penguin-vetiver-model-data/ --recursive --profile dev-deploy ``` ::: We can also see the `Python/` and `R/` in the dashboard under **Amazon S3** > **Buckets** ![Click to enlarge S3 bucket with penguin model data](img/lab7-s3-bucket-upload.png){width='100%' fig-align='center'} ## Pushing model data I've create a Quarto documents for each respective R and Python `vetiver` model: * [py_model.qmd](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab07/py_model.md) * [r_model.qmd](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab07/r_model.md) To push the `vetiver` model data when it rebuilds, we will have to adapt the 'Write to Local Board` sections: ### Write to Local Board (`Python`) The original code for writing the model out to a local directory in Python is below:[^py-orig] [^py-orig]: View original ['Write to Local Board' Python section.](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab07/py_model.md#write-to-local-board) ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} from pins import board_folder from vetiver import vetiver_pin_write board = board_folder("Python/models", allow_pickle_read=True) vetiver_pin_write(board, v) ``` ::: We can see the confirmation that the model was written to the local board: ```{.default} Model Cards provide a framework for transparent, responsible reporting. Use the vetiver `.qmd` Quarto template as a place to start, with vetiver.model_card() Writing pin: Name: 'penguin_lab07_model' Version: 20260710T065219Z-91fdd ``` ### Write to S3 Bucket (`Python`) To write this model data to the S3 bucket, we'll need to make the following changes: :::: {.callout-note collapse='true' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [Python Environment Variables]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.10em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} Python environment variables are set at the OS/shell level or loaded via `.env` files with libraries like `python-dotenv`. Python reads them using `os.environ` or `os.getenv()`. 1. Create a `.env` file in your project root: ```bash AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key AWS_REGION=us-east-1 ``` 2. Install `python-dotenv`: ```bash pip install python-dotenv ``` 3. Load it in your script: ```python from dotenv import load_dotenv import os load_dotenv() access_key = os.getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID") secret_key = os.getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY") region = os.getenv("AWS_REGION") ``` 4. Add `.env` to `.gitignore`. ::: :::: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} from dotenv import load_dotenv import os from pins import board_s3 from vetiver import vetiver_pin_write load_dotenv() board = board_s3(path="penguin-vetiver-model-data/Python/models", allow_pickle_read=True) vetiver_pin_write(board, v) ``` ::: ```{.default} Model Cards provide a framework for transparent, responsible reporting. Use the vetiver `.qmd` Quarto template as a place to start, with vetiver.model_card() Writing pin: Name: 'penguin_lab07_model' Version: 20260710T065220Z-91fdd ``` We can confirm it was uploaded with: ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="false"} print(board.pin_list()) ``` ::: ```{.default} ['penguin_lab07_model', 'penguin_model'] ``` We can see the Python model data has been pushed to the S3 bucket in the **AWS Console**: ![Click to enlarge Python vetiver model in S3 Bucket](img/lab7-aws-python-write-model-s3.png){width='100%' fig-align'center'} ### Write to Local Board (`R`) In `r_model.qmd`, we use the following to write the model data to a local board:[^r-orig] [^r-orig]: View original ['Write to Local Board' R section.](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab07/r_model.md#write-to-local-board) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} model_board <- pins::board_folder("R/models") vetiver::vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v) ``` ::: We can see the confirmation that the model was written to the local board: ```{.default} #> Creating new version '20260710T152331Z-09946' #> Writing to pin 'penguin_lab07_model' #> #> Create a Model Card for your published model #> • Model Cards provide a framework for transparent, responsible reporting #> • Use the vetiver `.Rmd` template as a place to start ``` ### Write to S3 Bucket (`R`) To write the `vetiver` model data to the S3 bucket using R, use the following: :::: {.callout-note collapse='true' appearance='default' icon='false'} ## [R Environment Variables]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.10em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 1.00em; color: #282b2d;'} R environment variables can be set in `.Renviron` files (user or project level) or via `Sys.setenv()` in a script. R reads them using `Sys.getenv()`. 1. Create a `.Renviron` file in your project root: ```bash AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your_access_key AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your_secret_key AWS_REGION=us-east-1 ``` 2. Restart R session to load `.Renviron`. 3. Access variables in your script: ```r access_key <- Sys.getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID") secret_key <- Sys.getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY") region <- Sys.getenv("AWS_REGION") ``` 4. Add `.Renviron` to `.gitignore`. ::: :::: You might need the `paws.storage` package installed to write to the S3 board. Install it with the following command: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # install.packages("paws.storage") ``` ::: `pins::board_s3()` will create a connection to the S3 bucket using the environment variables. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} s3_board <- pins::board_s3( bucket = "penguin-vetiver-model-data", prefix = "R/models/", region = Sys.getenv("AWS_REGION"), access_key = Sys.getenv("AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"), secret_access_key = Sys.getenv("AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY") ) vetiver::vetiver_pin_write(s3_board, v) ``` ::: ```{.default} #> Creating new version '20260710T152331Z-09946' #> Writing to pin 'penguin_lab07_model' ``` We can confirm this with `pins::pin_list()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} pins::pin_list(s3_board) ``` ::: ```{.default} #> [1] "penguin_lab07_model" "penguin_model" ``` We can see this model data has been pushed in the **AWS Console**: ![Click to enlarge R vetiver model in S3 Bucket](img/lab7-aws-r-write-model-s3.png){width='100%' fig-align'center'}
